ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as revised); Measures for Beneficial Owner Registration and Administration of Legal Persons and Other Organizations (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Administrative Measures for Market Entity Registration; and PBOC AML/CFT implementing rules. Under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, a beneficial owner is any individual who ultimately owns or controls a market entity through direct or indirect equity or voting rights of not less than 25%, or who exercises actual control by other means.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders, authorised signatories, beneficial controllers and counterparties must be screened before incorporation against domestic PEP registries and sanctions lists maintained by PBOC, SAMR, MOFCOM and the Ministry of Public Security, as well as against OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists. Additional adverse-media, enforcement-action, and politically-exposed-person screening is mandatory. Positive matches require immediate escalation to the AML Compliance Committee, asset freeze action if applicable, refusal or termination of the formation engagement, and full documentation with a timestamped electronic audit trail retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Independent Declaration and Registration Portal (Enterprise Name Self-Service System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory Simplified Chinese script; no Arabic numerals, Latin letters, or foreign words may appear in the statutory Chinese name except where expressly permitted for a WFOE trade name after approval. The name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division plus unique distinctive name plus industry description plus legal form, i.e., limited liability company. A foreign investor may use a registered Chinese transliteration of its corporate name, whether pinyin-based or customary, provided the transliteration is consistent with the foreign name and does not mislead the public. Any English-language short name is ancillary only and cannot replace the registered Chinese name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant will receive a written reason from the SAMR name clearance portal. The applicant may, within 15 working days from the rejection notice, request review by the same registration authority, or may re-submit a fresh name declaration with a modified distinctive element. If the review is denied, or no decision is issued within 10 working days, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next-higher SAMR authority within 60 days, and thereafter administrative litigation with the competent People's Court within 15 days of the reconsideration decision or 6 months from the original administrative act. The appeal must include the name clearance certificate, the rejection notice, the proposed Chinese name, the foreign investor's name authorization, and evidence of the intended business scope.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered address for a WFOE engaged in data center colocation and bare-metal server hosting. SAMR registration requires a genuine physical lease agreement, landlord ownership documentation, and a site inspection report demonstrating that the actual servers, cooling, power, and network equipment will be installed at the registered address. Local tax authorities require the registered address to be the actual place of business for VAT, corporate income tax, and invoice issuance; banks require physical presence for KYC and corporate settlement account opening. A virtual office will likely be rejected by banks and tax bureaus, and may be treated as false registration under market entity registration regulations, exposing the WFOE to fines, account freezing, and loss of qualified business status.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: high, with an estimated 75% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of formation for data center colocation businesses due to data-residency, cybersecurity, and fire-safety considerations. Inspection checklist: (1) original lease or ownership certificate for the registered premises; (2) actual server racks and colocation hardware present on site; (3) backup power supply and cooling logs; (4) fire suppression and environmental control compliance; (5) personnel badges and physical access controls; (6) network connectivity and equipment labeling; (7) invoices and VAT system available at the site; (8) UBO and corporate records accessible. Municipal tax, SAMR, and public security cybersecurity departments may coordinate for unannounced checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 1, 4, 15, 23, 24, 26, 27, 33, 40, 43, 46, 49, 51, 53, 59, 64, 68, 81, 87, 90, 97, 177, 181, 183, 190 and 197; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 15, 18, 22, 31, 37 and 38; Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law; Regulation on the Foreign Investment Information Reporting (SAMR/MOFCOM 2019).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Supervision Administration of the municipal district where the registered office is located, acting through the National Enterprise Registration and Integrated Online Government Service Platform (www.gjzwfw.gov.cn and gd.gsxt.gov.cn).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company, together with the Articles of Association, board resolutions and the legal representative declaration, submitted to the State Administration for Market Regulation or its local delegated office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The PRC Company Law does not require a minimum paid-up registered capital for a general WFOE limited liability company. The registered capital amount and the contribution schedule are recorded in the articles of association. Capital contributions must be in the subscribing shareholder's own name, denominated in RMB or a convertible currency, remitted into a dedicated capital contribution bank account opened in the company's name at an authorised bank in China, and verified by the receiving bank. There is no statutory requirement for an escrow or blocked account at the stage of incorporation, but once a capital account is opened, funds cannot be withdrawn except for lawful operational purposes and must be reported to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND INITIAL BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY. This written resolution is made on the date set out in the signature block by all shareholders and all initial directors of the Company pursuant to the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Articles of Association, and the conduct of this written resolution is a lawful substitute for a general meeting of the members and for a board meeting. WHEREAS the Company is promoted for incorporation as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise in the People's Republic of China for the purpose of data centre colocation, server rack space leasing and bare-metal server hosting; and the formation dossier, including the Articles of Association, the business scope statement, the registered office lease and the list of initial statutory officers, has been prepared by the formation counsel and examined by the founding shareholders; and the establishment of the Company is within the permitted category of the Foreign Investment Negative List. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online portal: National Electronic Tax Service Platform (e-Tax, https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the WFOE, after obtaining a business license from the Administration for Market Regulation, the enterprise automatically receives a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) which functions as the tax identification number (TIN). Within 30 days of incorporation, the entity must complete tax registration through the e-Tax portal, uploading the business license, corporate articles, legal representative identity documents, and bank account information. The system will assign VAT general/small-scale taxpayer status based on the projected annual turnover. For a foreign non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in China, apply for tax registration at the local STA bureau where the payer is located or through the non-resident tax code procedure under the applicable double tax treaty, submitting the certificate of residence and income tax withholding registration forms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (annual turnover threshold for mandatory general VAT taxpayer status; all incorporated entities are required to register for VAT upon establishment regardless of turnover)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the issuance of all VAT invoices through the official electronic invoice system (e-Fapiao) integrated with the National e-Tax system. Special VAT invoices require cryptographic tax-control equipment or the fully digitalized e-invoice platform with real-time data reporting to the STA. There is no optional offline issuance; invoice data is cleared automatically and matched to VAT returns. Anti-fraud measures include digital signatures, a national tax-control chip, and strict invoice quota controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods is zero-rated upon submission of the export customs declaration and proof of foreign exchange settlement. For services, zero-rating applies only to offshore services that are fully consumed outside China (post-2018 VAT reform). Data center colocation leasing is generally a domestic service subject to standard VAT rates; however, if the contract is with an offshore non-resident enterprise and the server equipment is located in a comprehensive bonded zone or the service is physically delivered abroad, it may qualify for zero-rating. The statutory tests are: (1) service is performed outside China; (2) both service recipient and usage are located outside China; (3) payment is in foreign currency and repatriated; and (4) no domestic taxable consumption occurs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form (export customs declaration record with customs seal)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (showing the goods are physically leaving China)
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (Inward Remittance Certificate / export foreign exchange verification form)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under China's export tax refund administration, any false or unsubstantiated zero-rating claim is deemed tax fraud. The tax authority may claw back the entire VAT refund, impose a penalty ranging from 50% to 5 times the refund amount, suspend export tax refund eligibility, and transfer criminal liability to the Public Security Bureau for prosecuted cases. The statutory audit statute of limitations is 10 years for cases involving fraudulent refund or tax evasion, and the company will be downgraded on the tax credit rating scale, restricting invoice quotas and export filing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBC); State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains separate current-account and capital-account convertibility regimes. Current-account transactions, including trade in goods and services, dividends, royalties and operating remittances, are generally convertible subject to authentic documentation and SAFE reporting; banks operate on a verify-before-process basis using the Trade Monitoring System. Export proceeds are no longer subject to mandatory conversion quotas; a WFOE may retain foreign currency in its domestic foreign exchange settlement account or sell it to a licensed bank at the prevailing market rate, provided that the export documentary trail, customs declarations and receipt records are complete. Capital-account transactions, including equity injection by the overseas parent, foreign debt and liquidation or profit distribution, require SAFE registration, dedicated capital accounts, and compliance with the negative list for foreign investment. The principal profit remittance hurdle is not exchange-control approval but proof of distributable profits: audited statutory financial statements, tax clearance, shareholder resolution and bank-level distribution reporting. The RMB exchange rate is managed with reference to a basket of currencies, and onshore spot transactions observe daily fluctuation bands. Surrender requirements have been liberalized; the PBC and SAFE may still impose macro-prudential adjustment factors on cross-border financing and short-term foreign debt, but ordinary trade proceeds are not forcibly converted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign currency receipts in China today. Under the goods trade foreign exchange administration framework, an A-class enterprise must repatriate export proceeds into its domestic foreign exchange settlement account within 180 days from the customs export declaration date, or within the extended period accepted by SAFE for valid commercial reasons, after which the funds may either be retained in foreign currency or converted into RMB at any licensed bank. B-class and C-class enterprises are subject to stricter bank verification, documentary reconciliation and, where required, SAFE confirmation before conversion or repatriation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary account-holding rail. Foreign digital EMI providers such as Revolut, Airwallex and Currencycloud are not licensed by the PBC or SAFE as deposit-taking institutions and cannot legally maintain a settlement or clearing account in the name of a PRC WFOE. They may be used only as auxiliary cross-border payment gateways through a licensed Chinese payment institution or bank, and even then their services are more relevant to e-commerce receipts than to the monthly ACH/SWIFT treasury operations of a data center colocation business. The WFOE must maintain its core settlement and capital accounts at a PRC commercial bank while using correspondent banking corridors for foreign-currency flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance of the legal representative and at least one authorized financial signatory is mandatory when opening a corporate settlement account for a newly incorporated WFOE. Remote digital onboarding and consular proxy opening are not generally accepted for the initial account activation; some banks may permit a local manager to appear in person with a notarized and China-legalized power of attorney if the foreign legal representative is non-resident, but the in-branch interview requirement remains a condition precedent for the banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity involving offshore intermediate holding companies, nominee shareholders, or trust structures above the WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A legalized corporate chain-of-title from the ultimate natural person shareholder to the WFOE, including certificates of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, share registers, director registers, UBO declarations, passport copies in notarized translation, group auditor confirmations, and bank reference letters for each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apparent inconsistency between the data center colocation business model and the projected payment geography, especially where rent invoices are generated for tenants in high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed colocation agreements, master service agreements, data center sublease or ownership deeds, rack and cabinet allocation records, server asset registers, utility and power-consumption invoices, carrier neutrality agreements, tenant KYC profiles, and a 12-month cash-flow forecast tying each tenant receivable to the corresponding colocation contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party or transit payment patterns in which rental or settlement funds are received from entities not named as the contractual lessee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A beneficiary and source-of-funds declaration for every third-party payment, the full contractual chain authorizing the payment, board resolutions from both the WFOE and the paying party, audited financial statements, bank statements evidencing the origin of the funds, and a transaction rationale memorandum approved by the WFOE compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP or adverse-media exposure arising from the foreign shareholder, any intermediate entity, or a material tenant operating in a restricted or high-risk territory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions screening results against the United Nations, OFAC, EU, and Chinese regulatory published lists, PEP and adverse-media reports for all shareholders, directors and material counterparties, sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, corporate transparency declarations, and the bank's enhanced due diligence committee approval where red flags remain unresolved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas parent must first complete SAFE foreign direct investment (FDI) basic information registration through the receiving PRC bank. The WFOE opens a capital-account-based FDI settlement account at the chosen tier-1 bank. The parent then remits the registered capital via SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary defined as the WFOE, the beneficiary bank account tagged to the SAFE capital account, and the payment purpose field referencing the FDI registration code and the purpose label 'Registered Capital / FDI Capital Injection'. The receiving bank validates the transaction against the capital account policy, ensures the underlying BOP code is a capital-account direct investment code rather than a current-account trade code, and records the receipt. After the funds clear, a PRC-registered accounting firm issues the capital verification report confirming paid-in capital. Subsequent RMB settlement of the foreign-currency capital is allowed for bona fide operating expenditures under the FDI capital settlement negative list, which prohibits use for prohibited investments, non-self-use real estate, and unauthorised equity investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For monthly rental collections and ordinary domestic vendor disbursements, the WFOE can use China's ACH-style small-amount bulk payment system with approved batch files. For overseas tenants or cross-border working-capital vendor payments, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 backed by invoices, purchase orders and customs declarations. For high-value imports of server equipment, precision cooling systems and electrical infrastructure, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (MT700) issued by the PRC bank is the preferred settlement rail because it protects both the WFOE and the equipment vendor. For standardized machinery or repeated component purchases, documentary collections (CAD/DP) can be used where shipping title documents are transferred through banking channels. All outbound trade payments must be reported under the correct BOP transaction code, reconciled with import verification records and cleared through either the CIPS network for RMB or the SWIFT correspondent banking system for USD, EUR and other convertible currencies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts with genuine trade or capital exposure, supported by SAFE-validated documentary evidence and bank ISDA documentation
Onshore FX swaps and rolling forwards used to align the timing of foreign-currency capital injection, monthly RMB lease collections and scheduled overseas capex disbursements
Cross-currency interest rate swaps matched to long-term data center financing where the notional and tenor cover only the underlying loan or lease liability

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not a permissible instrument for the onshore WFOE; any NDF-based hedge must be executed by the non-resident parent outside China and cannot involve conversion or settlement through the WFOE's onshore capital account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each calendar year for the preceding fiscal year ended December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 places the WFOE on the Abnormal Operating List; after three consecutive years, it is transferred to the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, exposing the entity to administrative strike-off, registration revocation, and legal representative disqualification. No separate late fee, but public credit penalties apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Return (Annual CIT Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) - local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 in the year following each December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax; late filing penalties range from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 (or up to 100% of unpaid tax in evasion cases); chronic delinquency enables enforced bank account attachment and tax deregistration, and may trigger SAMR automated strike-off for over 6 months of non-operating status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (Foreign Investment Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) accepted simultaneously through SAMR's annual report portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each year; within 30 days after any substantial change in foreign-investor equity or contributing information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report after administrative instruction leads to penalties under the Foreign Investment Law, including a fine of up to RMB 200,000, a public violation record, and potential denial of preferential tax and customs treatment; no automatic strike-off, but the adverse record cascades to the SAMR abnormal list.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR for the registration file and STA for the tax file; retained with the company's annual corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared after fiscal year end and physically completed by April 30 preceding the annual enterprise report submission; final audited statements must be available for the June 30 annual report attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company law non-audit exposure imposes fines on the company and directors; the auditor's refusal to sign a clean opinion triggers SAMR abnormal-risk flags and tax filing audit; repeated absence of an audit may support administrative deregistration. No direct government filing fee.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 164 of the PRC Company Law, every limited liability company must engage an independent licensed Chinese CPA firm to audit its annual financial statements. No balance-sheet total, turnover, or headcount threshold exempts a WFOE from the mandatory audit. For data-center colocation lessors, the low-risk data processing and service line does not change the mandate. In practice all WFOEs are audited without exception, and quantitative triggers beyond registration are not tax size-based but entity-type-based.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS), converged with IFRS, applicable to all WFOEs required to issue true and fair annual financial statements. Small-scale enterprises may use the Simplified or Intermediate Accounting Standards, but for tax and SAMR purposes, full CAS is customary for foreign-invested entities. Corporate income tax calculations are adjusted per the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Filing, a WFOE must file beneficial-owner details to SAMR within 30 days of formation or any change, and must update annual report data each year during the annual reporting window from January 1 through June 30. There is no separate standalone annual UBO relicensing fee; the 30-day change window is absolute for shareholding transfers, and share transfers also require notarized agreements, PRC tax declaration, and register entries. Failure to update within 30 days carries administrative fines and abnormal-list threat.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Legal Representative

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for registered agent, correspondence address, and annual SAMR reporting support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 18,000 per year depending on business volume, intercompany transactions, and data-center asset scale

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory data-center-specific tax holiday exists; standard CIT is 25%. Preferential 15% rate applies to qualifying encouraged industries in Western China and certain special zones. R&D expenditures of a qualifying WFOE may claim a 100% super deduction. Qualified technology transfer income up to RMB 5 million is exempt and the excess is taxed at an effective rate of 12.5%. No patent box regime is available for pure server colocation leasing, but qualifying high/new technology enterprise status may reduce CIT to 15% if the WFOE satisfies the statutory R&D and tech-income ratios.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Class A) with supporting schedules A105000, A105080, A107012, and A105050, filed through the provincial eTax electronic filing system of the State Taxation Administration by the WFOE legal representative and tax handler.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement (annual return and true-up) plus provisional quarterly returns filed on the same eTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Provisional CIT returns and quarterly payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter. The annual return must be filed and the final settlement completed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., by May 31 for a calendar-year WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter gross operating revenue from the WFOE's principal data center colocation activity, including rack space leasing, power metering and recovery, bare-metal hosting, managed services, and cross-connect or bandwidth auxiliary charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue must be recognized on an accrual basis and stripped of directly refundable outlays. For services performed by the PRC WFOE for overseas group companies, source and permanent-establishment attribution rules apply; the revenue reflected must be at arm's length and supported by written intercompany agreements, allocation keys, and contemporaneous evidence if the foreign counterparty is a related party. Do not omit revenue paid via SWIFT or cross-border ACH into offshore accounts; bank wires from overseas related parties are audit triggers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include direct data center operating costs: electricity, network bandwidth, cooling, facility depreciation and amortization, colocation equipment lease charges, hardware consumption, maintenance, and salaries of operations engineers directly attributable to the colocation lines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capitalized server racks, cooling systems and leasehold improvements must not be expensed currently. Cross-border service charges from a foreign parent are deductible only to the extent the services are actually rendered, benefit the WFOE, and are priced under the arm's length standard. If a related party charges for services already performed by local WFOE staff, the cost claim will be disallowed in full.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter non-CIT taxes and surcharges included in operating profit, such as urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, property tax, land use tax, stamp duty, and employment surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIT itself, VAT, and late payment surcharges are not deductible. If the WFOE pays property tax and land use tax on the hosting facility, those should be supported by title or lease documents; lease payments to a non-resident lessor may trigger rental WHT and should be scrutinized in reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include marketing and sales expenses for procuring data center capacity clients, advertising, commissions to sales agents, travel, and channel development for colocation contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions paid to an overseas related-party sales agent must satisfy benefit and arm's length tests; the payer must withhold VAT and income tax on Chinese-source services if the agent renders services in China. Accrued but unpaid commissions to offshore intermediaries without physical substance are a common base-erosion red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include general management, human resources, legal and professional fees, insurance, office expenses, and overhead not directly allocated to colocation operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party management fees require contractual specificity, actual service performance, and arm's length pricing; generic 'head office support' fees from the foreign parent without supporting work papers are disallowed and may be treated as disguised dividends. Legal fees for tax structuring and offshore trademark transfers must be separately identified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record interest expense on bank loans and related-party loans, financing fees, exchange differences, and other financial costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident related lenders is subject to statutory 10% WHT unless a DTA reduces it, and deductibility is capped by the thin-capitalization debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for a non-financial enterprise. If the WFOE fails to withhold on cross-border interest, the interest deduction may be denied and withholding penalties imposed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute total profit as business revenue less cost of services, taxes, selling, administrative and financial expenses, adjusted for gains/losses on asset disposals, non-operating income and non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Total accounting profit must reconcile with the audited financial statements used for the WFOE's investment book. Transfer pricing adjustments by the tax authority, unreported intercompany revenue, and excessive related-party charges will increase taxable income here; directors must ensure the reconciliation is documented or criminal falsification exposure arises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Lines 11-15) - Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter non-deductible permanent difference adjustments, temporary timing differences, tax losses carried forward, taxable income, applicable tax rate, and CIT payable before and after foreign tax credits and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 5-year loss carryforward is applied only in chronological order. Foreign tax credit relief, where the WFOE receives foreign-source income, must be supported by TRC and tax payment vouchers. If the WFOE benefits from DTA-reduced WHT on outbound dividends, that withholding is a separate obligation of the payer and is not a substitute for CIT payable on this return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late return filing under TCAL Article 62 triggers an administrative penalty of RMB 2,000, increased to RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases, plus late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on the outstanding CIT. Underpayment due to false bookkeeping attracts recovery, daily surcharge, and a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Deliberate fraud in the amount of five million RMB or more, or supporting false invoices, may constitute criminal tax evasion under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to seven years and fines. Failure to file is also a factor for the tax authority's negative credit blacklist, which triggers exit control through the joint disciplinary mechanism.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by the WFOE to a non-resident enterprise shareholder where the dividends are paid from post-CIT profits, unless the applicable Double Tax Agreement (DTA) provides a reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief for outbound dividends, the non-resident shareholder must submit a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of its jurisdiction of residence, together with a completed 'Information Report on Non-resident Taxpayers Enjoying Treaty Benefits' through the eTax system. The WFOE as withholding agent must collect and retain beneficial ownership evidence demonstrating that the foreign parent is the true recipient and not a conduit or contractual pass-through, especially where the parent is incorporated in Hong Kong or Singapore. Substantiation includes the foreign shareholder's board resolution authorizing the dividend, ownership certificate showing the 25% or more shareholding threshold for a 5% treaty rate, audited financial statements, evidence of economic activity in the residence state, and confirmation that the parent has legal authority to use and enjoy the dividend. The treaty rate is not self-executing: the reduced rate may be applied at the time of remittance only after the information report, TRC and beneficial ownership file are in place; if the documents are incomplete, the full 10% must be withheld and a refund application can later be made.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate for outbound interest and royalties is 10% under the Enterprise Income Tax Law for non-resident enterprises without a Chinese permanent establishment. Under China's DTA network, interest treaty rates typically range from 5% to 10% and royalty rates from 5% to 10%, depending on the treaty partner and intellectual property type; for example, the Mainland-Hong Kong arrangement commonly allows 7% on interest and 7% on royalties in qualifying circumstances, while certain treaties reduce interest to 5% for financial institutions or royalties to 5% for industrial patent payments. The same TRC, beneficial ownership and information-report protocol applies to interest and royalties; the WFOE must also source VAT on cross-border royalties at 6% plus local surcharges, although the VAT treatment is separate from CIT withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File contemporaneous documentation is mandatory if annual related-party tangible asset transactions equal or exceed RMB 200 million; if intangible property transfer/licensing reaches RMB 100 million; if financial asset transactions reach RMB 100 million; or if any other related-party transactions reach RMB 40 million. A Master File is required when the total annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion, or under the SAT's special adjustment rules where the enterprise's related-party transaction amount is material relative to its scale.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law applies a substance-over-form doctrine; the WFOE must demonstrate that its core income-generating activities (CIGA) are performed in China, including active oversight of data center rack capacity, client onboarding, power and network operation, troubleshooting, billing, and contract management. For DTA and anti-abuse purposes, a WFOE that is merely a booking shell, with directors in the parent state and all operational decisions made offshore, may be disregarded under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Article 47-48 of the EIT Law) and SAT guidelines. To claim the reduced dividend withholding rate, the foreign ultimate parent must separately have real economic substance as owner of the shares, not merely hold a nominee or conduit interest. The data center colocation business itself must also maintain physical presence, utility contracts, employment records, insurance policies, and board meetings in China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Bookkeeping of Data Center Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting an A100000 return that understates or omits revenue from cross-border rack space leasing and bare-metal hosting, or uses fake invoices and offshore receivable accounts to shift profit to a low-tax jurisdiction while keeping the WFOE nominally in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection (TCAL), tax authorities shall recover the underpaid CIT and impose a penalty of 50% to five times the tax underpaid, in addition to daily late surcharges of 0.05%. If the underpayment is deliberately concealed, it constitutes criminal tax evasion under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, exposing the entity to fines and imprisonment of up to seven years for those criminally liable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general managers and actual controlling persons may be personally liable where the corporate veil is pierced because the WFOE is a mere instrument or was used fraudulently; company assets, personal assets and restitution for unpaid taxes and interest may be reached. The legal representative may be placed on the tax authority's non-payer blacklist, which triggers travel restrictions, exit bans by border authorities, and disqualification from serving as senior management in any other Chinese entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Economic Substance Abuse (Shell Structure)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into fictitious or inflated management fee, royalty, and technology service agreements with the foreign parent or its subsidiaries; maintaining no real staff, power consumption data, client contracts, or operational decision-making in China; and applying an unadjusted cost-plus allocation or a misused TNMM to justify cross-border payments that do not match the colocation activity's economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in Articles 47 and 48, the tax authority may re-characterize the transactions, disregard the artificial structure, adjust taxable income, and assess additional CIT plus special tax adjustment interest. Where the arrangement is accompanied by false invoices or deliberate concealment, TCAL Article 63 imposes a 50% to five-times penalty and Criminal Law Article 201 may apply. The failure to prepare Local/Master File documentation when the threshold is met is separately penalized under TCAL and may be treated as non-compliance with the arm's length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A finding of sham status permits tax authorities and courts to pierce the corporate veil and recover underpaid tax from shareholders and directors who participated in the artificial structure; civil asset restitution from personally held property is available. The legal representative and relevant directors are also subject to the joint disciplinary blacklist, travel bans on leaving Chinese mainland, and potential criminal liability for evasion where the TP abuse was knowingly concealed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and DTA Benefit Fraud on Outbound Dividends, Interest and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, intercompany interest payments, or intellectual property royalties to the non-resident parent or a related party without withholding the statutory 10% WHT, or using forged, expired or inappropriate Tax Residency Certificates and shell conduit companies to claim a 5% DTA dividend rate or reduced interest/royalty rate without genuine beneficial ownership and substance in the treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 69 of TCAL, a withholding agent that fails to withhold and remit tax is liable to recover the tax and to a penalty of 50% to three times the tax not withheld; late surcharges continue to accrue. The enterprise may also be denied deduction of the underlying interest or royalty, and the non-resident's treaty relief claim may be retrospectively denied with full tax and interest assessed. Where the WFOE deliberately uses layered offshore entities and false documentation to evade WHT, the conduct is a criminal offense with imprisonment up to seven years under Criminal Law Article 201, and the movement of the funds abroad may separately trigger money-laundering liability under Criminal Law Article 191.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize the unwithheld distribution or sign false beneficial ownership declarations can be held personally liable after piercing of the corporate veil, especially where the distribution renders the WFOE insolvent or the restructuring existed to strip assets. Personal civil restitution covers unpaid WHT, penalties, surcharges and interest; the relevant individuals are Blacklisted by the tax and foreign exchange authorities, restrained from traveling outside China, and face imprisonment for tax fraud or laundering the repatriated profits if criminal fraud is established.
